dek: Allen Iverson played bigger than everybody on the floor. Why No. 3 is still the reason so many of us love the game.

slides.label: The size
slides.text: Listed at *6 feet and 165 pounds*, Allen Iverson went No. 1 in the 1996 draft. In 2001 he became the *shortest and lightest MVP* in NBA history.

slides.label: The heart
slides.text: Four scoring titles. *11 All-Star* nods. *31.1 points* a night in his MVP season, taking hits from men a foot taller and getting *right back up*.

slides.label: The crossover
slides.text: March 12, 1997. A rookie at the top of the key looked at *Michael Jordan* and crossed him anyway. *Respect the giant. Never fear him.*

slides.label: The practice
slides.text: In 2002 the world laughed at *"we talkin' about practice."* The braids, the ink, the honesty. He never shrank himself to make a room *comfortable*.

slides.label: The comeback
slides.text: At 17 he was locked up and written off. Clemency came, the conviction was *overturned*, and John Thompson gave him a shot at *Georgetown*.

slides.label: The Hall
slides.text: At his 2016 Hall of Fame speech he thanked everybody, even the friends who turned on him: *"I know the signs."* Betrayal is just *information*.

slides.label: The influence
slides.text: *LeBron* ranked A.I. right behind MJ. *Wade* wore No. 3 and the sleeve for him. *Melo* says he shaped his career. Wade and Melo both picked him to *present them* at the Hall.

slides.label: Where it started
slides.text: For Den founder Danny Silverio: *1998*, Hamilton Fish Park and Forsyth with his cousin *Francisco Reynoso Jr.* Every touch of the ball, he was trying to be *A.I.*

question: Who made YOU fall in love with the game?

caption_instagram:
Allen Iverson was listed at 6 feet and 165 pounds, and he played bigger than everybody on the floor.

No. 1 pick in 1996. MVP in 2001, the shortest and lightest in league history. Four scoring titles, 11 All-Star nods and a rookie crossover on Michael Jordan nobody forgot. Locked up at 17 and written off, he came back through Georgetown and finished in the Hall of Fame, where he even thanked the friends who turned on him.

You can see him in the players who came after. LeBron James called A.I. his favorite player growing up after MJ. Dwyane Wade wore No. 3 and the arm sleeve because of him. Carmelo Anthony says Iverson impacted his whole career, and Wade and Melo both chose him to present them at the Hall.

For Den founder Danny Silverio, it started in 1998 on the courts at Hamilton Fish Park and Forsyth with his cousin Francisco Reynoso Jr., whose father played for team DR. "Every time I touched the ball, I was trying to be A.I. He taught me to play bigger than my size and never quit, even when life thinks you're down and out."

caption_linkedin:
Allen Iverson was listed at 6 feet and 165 pounds in a league built for giants. He still became the No. 1 pick, a four-time scoring champion and, in 2001, the shortest and lightest MVP in NBA history.

Three lessons that travel well beyond basketball:

1. Your size is not your ceiling. The measuring tape is someone else's opinion.
2. Be yourself in rooms that weren't built for you. Iverson never shrank to make anyone comfortable, and a generation of stars, from LeBron James to Dwyane Wade to Carmelo Anthony, grew up wanting to play like him.
3. Setbacks are seasons, not sentences. Written off at 17, he finished in the Hall of Fame.

For our founder Danny Silverio, it started in 1998 on the courts at Hamilton Fish Park, trying to be A.I. on every possession.
